messages:
kevin: Quick flag — tenant-123 flooded with SLO alerts last night. They got routed to both /eng-oncall and #tenant-123-ops which caused duplicate pages and lots of noise. Can we decide on a tenant-level alert affinity + quiet-backoff behavior? I sketched an API and some UX ideas below.

anya: Ugh, saw that. Duplicates are brutal for oncall. +1 to handling affinity at routing layer, not just console.

maria: Do we have telemetry on how often the duplicates happen vs true distinct signals? That will affect the backoff defaults.

kevin: Minimal numbers: tenant-123 generated ~22 alert events in a 2h window; 18 routed to both destinations. Suppressed_count was ~12 after our emergency dampening. We should track routed_count, suppressed_count, and avg_ack_latency per-tenant.

sam: API-level fields I was imagining: 
```
notify_affinity: ["tenant_channel", "eng_oncall"]
quiet_backoff_ms: 300000  # per-tenant default
fallback_policy: ["tenant_channel", "eng_oncall"]
allow_tenant_override: true
```
But need strong guardrails if tenants can override.

elena: UX: console should show a compact badge on the SLO alert that says "Affinity: tenant_channel → pause 5m" and let ops click to expand + edit. Also a global toggle for org admins to lock overrides.

maria: Instead of fixed quiet_backoff_ms, consider exponential backoff per-incident series: 1m, 2m, 5m, 15m. That reduces noise for flappy signals but still surfaces regressions.

kevin: I like exponential. Suggest default series [60, 120, 300, 900] (seconds). Add a hard upper bound and a bypass for severity=critical.

anya: Important: routing affinity should be idempotent and surface in telemetry so billing/alerts lines up. If we route to tenant first, we should mark routed_target and final_target in traces.

sam: Implementation notes: routing policy lives in notify-router service. New per-tenant config blob: 
```
{ "affinity_order": ["tenant_channel","eng_oncall"], "backoff_series": [60,120,300,900], "lock_overrides": false }
```
Router uses affinity_order to attempt send; if first target is already within backoff window we skip and try next. If none reachable, fall back to fanout to secondary tier.

elena: Console mapping: expose the backoff series and current suppression state. We should also show "recently suppressed" counter in the alert detail pane so owners know things were held.

maria: Edge case: cross-tenant incidents where many tenants correlate to same infra event. If every tenant suppresses then no one pages. We need a global override that can opt a tenant out of suppression when correlation_score > 0.7.

kevin: Good call. Add correlation_score check. If correlation >= 0.7 and severity >= major, bypass backoff.

devops-bot: Note: changing routing logic will affect existing incident playbooks. Please coordinate with SRE runbooks before rollout.

anya: Rollout plan idea: 1) add telemetry + dry-run mode (router logs intended target but doesn't apply backoff); 2) expose per-tenant defaults in console behind feature flag; 3) allow opt-in enforcement for early adopters; 4) GA with migration script to create defaults for all tenants.

sam: Concern: Migration script needs conservative defaults. Propose initially lock_overrides=true for enterprise tenants until we do manual outreach.

kevin: Action items:
- kevin: PR sketch for router config proto and telemetry fields (I'll do today).
- anya: design the console badge + edit flow (can you mock a compact state + expanded editor?)
- maria: propose backoff exponential tuning and correlation threshold heuristics.
- sam: draft migration + runbook notes for SRE.

elena: I'll volunteer to prototype the console badge microcopy and the admin lock UI.

alerts-bot: auto: routed-intent log created for tenant-123 at 1972507002 (dry-run).

devops-bot: ack: added SRE runbook check to the rollout checklist.

kevin: Great — thanks. If we can get PR + mock by EOD tomorrow we can start dry-run in staging next week.

sam: I'll coordinate runbook review with SRE.

kevin: Thanks all.
